concept.title: Printing and PDF
concept.shortdesc: Every page prints, or saves as PDF, from a browser on A4 by default; with govuk.print=yes the build also writes the whole publication as one file for printing end to end.

conbody.p: printingprint stylesheetprint documentPDFWebsites are the primary output, and GOV.UK guidance is to publish HTML first and PDF only as a last resort. The plugin follows that: nothing is bundled to make PDFs, but every page carries a print stylesheet, and a publication can be written as a single document that a browser prints whole. Building PDFs inside the toolkit, with page-numbered contents and index, is planned for release 1.1.

section.title: Printing a page
section.p: Use the browser's print or save-as-PDF command on any page. The print stylesheet hides the masthead, sidebar, search, pagination and footer, lays the content out in one column, keeps headings with the text that follows them, keeps tables, figures and code blocks whole where it can, repeats table headers across pages, and puts the page number in the bottom margin. Links to other websites print with their address after the link text, as the Design System's own print rules provide.

The paper size is set at build time with govuk.pdf.paper (A4 by default; also A5, A3, B5, B4, JIS-B5, JIS-B4, Letter, Legal and Ledger, or a width and height such as 148mm 210mm) and govuk.pdf.orientation (portrait by default, or landscape). Browsers offer their own paper choice in the print dialog as well; the build's setting is the default the page asks for. The same two parameters will drive the 1.1 PDF step, so a publisher sets them once.

section.title: The print document
section.p: Set govuk.print=yes and the build writes print.html beside index.html: the whole publication in one self-contained file, linked from the home page and from every footer as "Whole publication (print version)". It holds:

ul.li: a cover block with the publication's title, abstract and authorship from the bookmap or map;
a linked contents list, to govuk.print.toc.depth levels (3 by default);

every navigable topic in the map's reading order, rendered exactly as on its own page, with headings stepped down by its depth in the map so the document's outline is a single hierarchy — chapters, parts and appendices each start a new printed page;
footnotes gathered at the end of their topic;
the glossary and the index as final parts, their entries linking to the topics.

section.p: Every id the website uses is kept, so cross-references between topics become links within the document and the index resolves without page numbers. Topics excluded from navigation (toc="no") and resource-only references are left out; a topic reached from more than one place is included once. The file is never indexed by site search, so it cannot duplicate every result.

On screen it reads as one long single-column page — useful for offline reading, review circulation or archiving. Printed, or saved as PDF from a browser, it becomes the whole publication with running page numbers; Chromium-based browsers also produce a tagged PDF with a document outline from the headings. A publisher with a CSS Paged Media formatter can render the same file directly.

Very large publications are not one printable document. The build writes the file only when the publication has no more than govuk.print.max-topics topic files (500 by default); above that it reports GOVK003W and writes nothing, and no page links to it. Publications of that size can produce print documents per part by building their submaps, or leave printing to the per-page stylesheet.

section.title: What a browser cannot do yet
section.p: Browsers implement the paged parts of CSS unevenly, so at this release the contents list and index carry links rather than page numbers, footnotes appear as endnotes, and the accessibility tagging of a saved PDF is the browser's own. All three become page-numbered, footnoted and tagged to PDF/UA from the same file under the 1.1 PDF step, which adds a pure-Java CSS engine to the build with no other software to install. The design is recorded in the project's design folder as decision D-20.
